title: When the Bakery Turns
premise: Astrid Eastwick's quiet coastal life shatters when a letter her grandfather never mailed — dated eleven years ago, naming her the heir to the Holloway Bakery and its debts — surfaces in a dead solicitor's files. Returning to the town that once exiled her family, she clashes with Callum Voss, the baker who has kept the ovens warm in her absence and believes the inheritance is rightfully his. As they are forced to work one last season together, their rivalry softens into something neither can name, until Astrid discovers the letter was suppressed deliberately by the man who now runs the town. In the end, Astrid chooses to share the bakery rather than claim it alone, letting Callum stay past the last train as she boards the final ferry of the season — only to turn back at the dock.
about_author: Wendell Ravensworth is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who wrote his first novel during long fog-bound watches off the northern coast. He now lives in a converted bakehouse, where he insists the smell of bread is essential to his process.

chapters.title: The Letter That Waited Eleven Years
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. While cataloguing her late grandfather's effects, Astrid finds an unmailed letter naming her heir to the Holloway Bakery — and hinting someone wanted it buried. She travels to the town that turned on her family years ago, where she meets Callum Voss, flour-dusted and furious at her arrival. The beat: reluctant homecoming, old wounds reopened, first spark of friction.

chapters.title: Proofing Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced by the estate's terms to run the bakery together through the tourist season, Astrid and Callum fall into an uneasy rhythm — her recipes, his hands, her insomnia, his patience. She begins drafting a novel about a town with a secret; he almost tells her his own. The beat: warmth growing in shared labor, trust tentatively rising like dough.

chapters.title: What Aldous Marrow Kept
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Callum discovers that Aldous Marrow, the town's patriarch and the bakery's creditor, intercepted the original letter to keep the Eastwick inheritance from surfacing — and that his own father helped bury it. When he confronts Marrow, he's offered the bakery outright if he turns Astrid out. The beat: betrayal and temptation, the corruption of power made personal, climax igniting.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Exposed by Callum's confession, Marrow's hold on the town cracks before an assembled crowd at the harvest festival, and the bakery's deed passes to both names. On the season's final day, Astrid boards the last ferry intending to return to her old life — then sees Callum waiting on the dock, having missed the last train to stay. The beat: resolution, forgiveness, belonging finally chosen over safety.
